signals.name: Byrne Hobart
signals.summary: A third-party digest dated Nov 7 lists a Diff longreads roundup covering quant funds, online subcultures and frontier AI, and the limits of private-market prediction exchanges. I haven't checked it against the original on thediff.co.

signals.name: Michael Burry
signals.latest_title: Sold 25% of chip puts, still very bearish
signals.summary: After the semiconductor ETF (SMH) fell about 11% on Nov 5, Burry told paid Cassandra Unchained subscribers he sold 25% of his SMH puts. He remains very bearish. This is secondhand coverage of his paywalled post.
signals.connection: Ties to the AI compute race and mega-valuations story and to falling stocks. It is a bearish counterpoint to the chip-spending boom.

signals.name: Ben Thompson
signals.latest_title: The Jensen Huang Story Gets Worse, Washington vs. New York, Silicon Valley
signals.summary: Thompson wrote two pieces this week on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a Chinese spy. He argues the bigger risk to Huang is governance, more than national security, and says Huang's influence will never be the same. The week's roundup also covered AI on the ballot, a Google state of the union, and China.
signals.connection: Bears on the AI compute race and on Nvidia's mega-valuation. It also touches US-China tech policy, AI governance and the post-election Washington shift.

signals.name: Paul Graham
signals.latest_title: Lightcone: How To Build The Future (with Amjad Masad)
signals.summary: Graham appeared on a YC Lightcone episode with Amjad Masad dated Nov 7. I only saw the listing, not the content. I found no posts of his own from the last 7 days.
signals.connection: Loosely tied to the AI-built software and startup theme. The link is weak.

signals.name: Packy McCormick
signals.summary: The weekly roundup of positive science and tech news covers plasmid DNA immunotherapy, Zipline, DREADDs and NOM4D, plus extra items.
signals.connection: Applied tech and industry. It is a counterweight to the market-selloff and political news.

signals.name: Lenny Rachitsky
signals.latest_title: State of the tech job market: late 2026
signals.summary: Lenny reports that product managers are doing well, engineers have plateaued and designers are struggling. He says the biggest AI hiring boom is outside software. He also posted a Fable 5.2 video review, covering what it built and where it fell short, and a How I AI episode.
signals.connection: Directly on the labor and workforce topic and on AI's effect on jobs. The Fable 5.2 review ties to frontier AI.
